body.statement: Determine the minimax order of \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\) in the two regimes not settled by the boundary and fixed-interior theorems: first, the balanced rank-one L-mask when the incoherence bound is allowed to depend on \(n\), with \(\mu=\mu(n)>1\) and \(\mu(n)\downarrow1\); second, arbitrary quantitatively admissible interior multi-chart wedges with fixed \(\mu>1\) and \(0<\kappa\le1\).  In each regime, determine whether a polynomial-time uniformly honest spectral certificate and a same-class all-procedure lower bound match.  No interpolation rate between the zero/\(\sigma\) boundary frontier and the fixed-interior \(\sigma\sqrt n\) frontier is asserted.
body.justification: The proved endpoints leave two mathematically distinct problems: the shrinking layer next to active incoherence and the geometry of arbitrary interior multi-chart wedges.
body.gap: Neither the boundary sign experiment nor the fixed-\(\mu>1\) one-block packing supplies a uniform interpolation theorem or a matching arbitrary-wedge certificate.
body.consumer: A solution would tell panel researchers when boundary discreteness ceases to dominate and whether general staggered wedges admit a computationally matched honest-radius frontier.

obligation.what_is_open: Characterize separately the shrinking-incoherence boundary layer and the fixed-interior arbitrary multi-chart wedge frontier, with matching honest upper and all-procedure lower bounds when possible.
obligation.obstruction: The boundary proof uses discrete sign recovery once incoherence is exactly active, whereas the interior proof uses continuous perturbations with slack. Neither argument is uniform as the slack vanishes, and no same-class tangent packing is available for every admissible multi-chart wedge.
obligation.attempted: The exact \(\mu=1\) reduction and the fixed-\(\mu>1\) one-block frontier determine the two endpoint regimes, but they do not determine an interpolation scale or control chart synchronization and mask amplification uniformly over general wedges.
